summary: A 1942 Aermotor steel fire tower from Jackson County, Ohio, donated and rebuilt in 2023 at Scioto Grove Metro Park, where it is now climbable.

facts.design: Aermotor Windmill Co. galvanized-steel tower with an internal staircase (the costliest of Aermotor's three climb styles)

access.note: Open to the public during daylight hours at its current site, Scioto Grove Metro Park; the original Jackson County site was on private land and reachable only with the owner's permission before the 2023 move.

visit.trail_note: 111 steps to the lookout cab floor, inside Scioto Grove Metro Park, Grove City, Ohio

facts.agency: Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks (current, since 2023)

events.note: Erected in Jackson County, Ohio by the Aermotor Windmill Company as a U.S. Forest Service fire tower with an internal staircase
NHLR visit report found it abandoned, vandalized, with the first flight of stairs removed; access only through private property
Taylor family donated the tower; dismantled, trucked ~75 miles in three sections, re-galvanized, and rebuilt at Scioto Grove Metro Park (Franklin County) for about $140,000
New stair treads and windows, safety fencing, and a rebuilt lookout cab added during the rebuild
Public grand opening at Scioto Grove Metro Park on August 15, 2023

evidence.supports: built 1942 by Aermotor as a USFS tower
evidence.quote: The Keystone Fire Tower was set up in Jackson County, Ohio in 1942, to help protect southern Ohio forests from wild fires.
This fire tower was built by the Aermotor Windmill Company, which became the most successful developer of metal windmills in the American Midwest.

evidence.supports: Aermotor based in Chicago; USFS contracted for galvanized-steel towers
evidence.quote: The US Forest Service installed fire towers across America and from the early 1920s contracted with Aermotor to develop fire towers constructed mainly of galvanized steel. The zinc coating from the hot dip galvanizing process prevents rust of the steel. The company, based in Chicago, developed three types of fire towers

evidence.supports: three Aermotor climb styles and costliest/internal staircase
evidence.quote: one with an outside ladder to the top, another with an inside ladder to the top, and the most expensive type, with an inside metal staircase.

evidence.supports: costliest of three Aermotor climb types, internal staircase
evidence.quote: The Keystone Fire Tower, the one now installed at Scioto Grove Metro Park, is of this latter type.
This is 45-foot high steel tower was originally located in southeastern Jackson County, Ohio .

evidence.supports: Metro Parks gives 82 feet to cab floor
evidence.quote: The tower rises 82 feet from ground to the floor of the lookout, and the steep but perfectly secure steps are not for the faint of heart.
First flight of stairs have been taken down presumably for safety reasons. The tower and surrounding area has been heavily vandalized by locals.
Access is through private property, so must ask for permission before entering.

evidence.supports: Taylor family donated the tower to Metro Parks
evidence.quote: The land on which the Keystone Fire Tower had been erected came into private ownership, and Justin Taylor, on behalf of the entire Taylor family, donated the fire tower to Metro Parks.

evidence.supports: cost ~$140,000, 3 sections, ~75 miles, re-galvanized, rebuilt at Scioto Grove
evidence.quote: This free gift actually cost Metro Parks about $140,000 to dismantle it in Jackson Country, transport it in three sections about 75 miles to its new location, galvanize it again and reassemble it onsite, while adding safety fencing and a completely rebuilt lookout structure at the top.

evidence.supports: new stair treads and windows added
evidence.quote: Refurbished by Metro Parks staff, the fire tower boasts new stair treads and windows, blending safety with a touch of rustic allure.
This carefully curated experience will be accessible to the public during daylight hours starting August 15, 2023
Adventure awaits you at Scioto Grove Metro Park, if you’re bold enough to climb the 111 rather steep steps to the top of the Fire Tower.

evidence.supports: view of Scioto River and Columbus skyline ~7 miles away
evidence.quote: A stunning view of the City of Columbus, about 7 miles away, is available from the top of the tower, as well as the surrounding park on the Scioto River.
By a happy stroke of coincidence, the 82-foot-high structure was transplanted to central Ohio 82 years after it was erected as a US Forest Service Fire Tower.

corrections.why: Sources date the dismantling, transport, and rebuild to 2023, with public opening August 15, 2023

sources.title: Are you bold enough to climb the fire tower?
sources.publisher: Metro Parks (Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks)

sources.title: The New Fire Tower At Scioto Grove Offers Stunning Views

notes_for_editor: Height is disputed between sources: NHLR's register entry (recorded 2014, pre-move) gives 45 feet; the Metro Parks blog (post-move, more detailed) gives 82 feet to the cab floor; Columbus Navigator says 100 feet overall. I used 82 ft (25.0 m) in facts.height_m as the most detailed account, and flagged the discrepancy in the story rather than silently picking one. The destination record us-oh-keystone-at-scioto-grove-metro-park may want the same height note and a built-1942 event added; not edited here since this task scoped only us-oh-keystone. Fact-check 2026-10-04: Columbus Navigator also attributes the donation to 'an anonymous private landowner', conflicting with the Metro Parks blog's naming of the Taylor family; the story follows the Metro Parks account only, which the evidence supports, but a human may want to reconcile this.
